'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**[[Baloch Liberation Army]] forces launch a multipronged attack dubbed "Operation Dara-e-Bolan" on [[Pakistan]]i security forces, capturing [[security checkpoint|checkpoints]] and Pakistani [[military base|bases]] in [[Machh]], and attacking other areas, including [[Kolpur]]. [https://thebalochistanpost.net/2024/01/major-offensive-in-balochistan-blas-elite-units-initiate-operation-dara-e-bolan/ (The Balochistan Post)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russia]] claims control of the village of [[Tabaivka]], but this is denied by [[Ukraine]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/russia-claims-capture-of-village-near-kupiansk-ukraine-denies/ (Kyiv Independent)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Chinese property sector crisis (2020–present)|Chinese property sector crisis]]
**The [[High Court of Hong Kong]] orders [[Evergrande Group]] into [[liquidation]] after the [[real estate developer]] fails to [[debt restructuring|restructure a debt]] amount in excess of {{US$|300}} billion. [https://apnews.com/article/china-evergrande-property-liquidation-order-7965ab1ec2f0208c53f9298daf8b9fd0 (AP)]
*[[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] terminates its proposed {{US$|1.7}} billion acquisition of consumer robot manufacturer [[iRobot|iRobot Corporation]] after facing [[antitrust]] scrutiny from the [[European Commission]]. [https://apnews.com/article/amazon-roomba-european-union-antitrust-decision-53bc9fdc780fa312cf6d83e2fdc96351 (AP)]
* [[CNN Philippines]] announces cessation of operations starting January 31, after broadcasting for nine years, due to financial losses by its [[parent company]] [[Nine Media Corporation]]. [https://asia.nikkei.com/Business/Media-Entertainment/CNN-Philippines-to-stop-broadcasting-after-9-year-run (''Nikkei Asia'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Iran–Israel proxy conflict]]
**Four men are [[Capital punishment|executed]] in [[Iran]] after being convicted of planning a [[bomb]] attack ordered by [[Israel]]’s [[Mossad]] agency on a factory making military equipment. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/1/29/iran-executes-four-men-convicted-of-spying-for-israel-state-media (Al Jazeera)]
**The man who claimed that he is the fugitive Satoshi Kirishima, a former member of the [[East Asia Anti-Japan Armed Front]] who was wanted for his role in a series of bombings in the 1970s and who was arrested by [[Japanese police]] on January 25, dies of [[cancer]] in a hospital in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]]. However, it has not been confirmed if the man was actually Kirishima. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20240129_12/ (NHK World)]
*Police arrest five people for the deaths of six people found in the desert near [[El Mirage, California|El Mirage]], [[California]], [[United States]], allegedly over an illegal [[Cannabis (drug)|marijuana]] trade. The victims were shot dead, with the bodies of four of them being burned. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/jan/29/police-arrests-bodies-desert-california (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 South African general election]]
**Former [[President of South Africa|President]] [[Jacob Zuma]] is suspended from the [[African National Congress]], the party he led from 2007 to 2017. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-68129365 (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*American [[neurotechnology]] company [[Neuralink]] announces it has implanted its [[brain–computer interface]] in a [[human]] brain for the first time, and that the person is "recovering well" with "initial results showing promising [[neuron]] spike detection". [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2024/jan/29/elon-musk-neuralink-first-human-brain-chip-implant (''The Guardian'')]
